main_body: Slate-roofed stall: a curved roof canopy on two wooden posts, with a gray stone water basin or counter below
top_band: Light blue-gray cap at rows 1-3, then the sloped roof surface in mid blue-gray with vertical ribs down to row 15. Lower basin: light gray rim at rows 30-31 over a blue water surface at rows 31-35.
evidence: The roof reads as a sloped surface with a lighter cap and a dark eave line at rows 15-17, and the posts sit set back beneath it. The basin shows a light rim, an inset water surface about 5 rows tall, and a gray front face at rows 36-42. Both a top surface and a front face are drawn, so it reads as 3/4 despite the roof ribs being vertical.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 steps and decent rib shading, comparable to the reference well roof. The posts are nearly flat orange with only an edge highlight, and the basin front is a large flat gray area (about 12x6 px) with no grain or speckle. The outlines are a dark neutral navy and brown, partly near-black. Many tiles (posts, basin front) carry only 2-4 colours, so it is thinner than the reference stall and well.
